steps.why: The inks are shared by every screen, so they live in tokens.json and reach the CSS through var().
Rozha One and Bricolage Grotesque come from the OFL library with their @font-face rules and are named by the font tokens.
A flat three-ink harbour print is drawn best as vector shapes with multiply blending, which reads as overprinted ink.
The ticket is a card component: a numbered body, a dashed perforation and a stub with the minutes.
The route of stops is a list component with done, current and next states on a dotted line.
Two one-shot keyframe animations, both removed under prefers-reduced-motion; neither loops, so no pause control is needed.
Titles, buttons, onboarding and progress text are rewritten in the warm, encouraging register around the fixed facts.

review.look: The welcome screen opens on a three-ink harbour print with a striped sun, hills, pier light and waves, the overprinted inks visibly blending, above a fat-face headline.
Each walk in the list reads as a numbered printed ticket with a dashed perforation and a stub showing its minutes, and the walk facts are legible.
Headlines are set in a heavy fat-face serif and body text in a grotesque, on cream stock with indigo ink and terracotta actions, consistently across all four screens.
The walk screen shows every stop as a stamp on a dotted line with visited, current and next clearly different.
Titles and buttons speak in a warm, passionate, encouraging voice without changing any walk fact.
